Definition: from a derivative of τρύγω (to dry) meaning ripe fruit (as if dry); to collect the vintage:--gather.
BiblicalUsage: trygáō names to collect the vintage. It appears 3 times in Scripture, including Luke 6:44 and Revelation 14:18.
TheologicalSignificance: My position: trygáō carries the precision of a God who says what He means.
